spec.title: Learning How to Learn
spec.project: Build a one-week learning plan, collect delayed evidence, and revise the plan from what happened.
constraints: Treat confidence as a prediction to check, not proof.
Use practice that produces inspectable evidence.

outcomes.title: Judge learning with evidence
outcomes.description: Separate a feeling of knowing from observable performance and calibration.

outcomes.title: Plan access to knowledge
outcomes.description: Use retrieval, useful cues, spacing, and interleaving for a concrete study target.

outcomes.title: Interpret productive effort
outcomes.description: Distinguish effort and chunk formation from false fluency.

outcomes.title: Use support that fades
outcomes.description: Learn from examples, explanations, feedback, and error analysis before attempting independently.

outcomes.title: Improve a learning routine
outcomes.description: Plan, reflect on delayed evidence, and adapt the next attempt.

kcs.name: Evidence of learning
kcs.description: A performance record is stronger evidence than a study feeling.

kcs.name: Calibration
kcs.description: Compare a confidence prediction with later performance.

kcs.name: Retention and transfer
kcs.description: Check later recall and application in a changed context.

kcs.name: Retrieval and cues
kcs.description: Attempt recall, then use a cue that points to the target without supplying it.

kcs.name: Spacing and interleaving
kcs.description: Distribute returns over time and mix related problem types when choosing a method matters.

kcs.name: Effort as information
kcs.description: Effort during retrieval can reveal what needs work; it is not by itself a grade of learning.

kcs.name: False fluency
kcs.description: Familiarity after rereading can feel like knowing without supporting later recall.

kcs.name: Chunking through meaningful structure
kcs.description: Group elements by a relationship you can explain and use, rather than by proximity alone.

kcs.name: Examples and scaffolding
kcs.description: Use a worked example or prompt as temporary support, then remove parts before independent work.

kcs.name: Self-explanation
kcs.description: Explain why a step follows from a principle, not merely what the step is.

kcs.name: Feedback and error analysis
kcs.description: Classify an error, correct it, and choose a next practice condition that can test the correction.

kcs.name: Learning plans
kcs.description: Choose a target, practice condition, and later check before starting.

kcs.name: Reflection from records
kcs.description: Use predictions, attempts, and results to identify a specific change.

kcs.name: Adaptation
kcs.description: Change the next learning action in response to evidence rather than repeating an untested routine.

content.positive: After studying five vocabulary terms, predict 4/5 tomorrow, hide the list, and record the actual score and use of one term in a new sentence.
content.negative: Read the list until all five terms look familiar, then record only ‘felt easy.’
content.explanation: The first creates a prediction, delayed retrieval marker, and changed-context application; the second does not distinguish familiarity from retention or transfer.

content.positive: On Monday retrieve the steps for a ratio problem; on Wednesday mix ratio and percentage problems, using ‘part-to-whole?’ only after an attempt stalls.
content.negative: Do all ratio problems in one block while rereading the formula whenever the answer is not immediate.
content.explanation: The first makes retrieval, a limited cue, a later return, and method selection visible.

content.positive: A learner groups a proof into claim, reason, and consequence, then explains the links from memory despite a pause.
content.negative: A learner highlights the proof twice and takes the smooth rereading experience as proof it can be reconstructed.
content.explanation: A pause is information to investigate; the meaningful groups and explanation provide a later test.

content.positive: First label why each step in a worked solution applies, then solve a similar problem with the reason prompts removed and classify any error as selection, execution, or explanation.
content.negative: Copy a worked solution, compare only the final number, and repeat the same problem unchanged.
content.explanation: Support is faded and feedback changes the next attempt rather than ending at correction.

content.positive: Plan two 10-minute retrieval attempts and a Friday check; after the record shows correct definitions but weak examples, add changed-context example practice next week.
content.negative: Plan to ‘study harder’ and keep the same routine after an unrecorded result.
content.explanation: A plan names evidence, reflection uses a record, and adaptation is a testable change.

misconceptions.name: Confidence proves learning
misconceptions.diagnostic_probe: If you are 95% confident immediately after reading, what evidence would show whether that prediction was calibrated tomorrow?
misconceptions.correction: Record a prediction, delayed retrieval result, and a changed-context use; confidence alone is not the evidence.

misconceptions.name: Rereading is the same as retrieval
misconceptions.diagnostic_probe: Which action asks you to produce an answer before seeing it: rereading a definition or covering it and recalling it?
misconceptions.correction: Retrieval requires an attempt before the answer; cues can be added after the attempt without replacing it.

misconceptions.name: Effort means failure
misconceptions.diagnostic_probe: Does a difficult recall attempt prove you learned nothing, or could it reveal a target for the next attempt?
misconceptions.correction: Effort is a signal to inspect with performance records; explainable structure can make later retrieval more usable.

misconceptions.name: Seeing a solution is enough
misconceptions.diagnostic_probe: After a worked example, what would show you can select and justify a step without its labels?
misconceptions.correction: Fade prompts, attempt a related case, and use feedback to classify and test a correction.

misconceptions.name: Reflection is just describing feelings
misconceptions.diagnostic_probe: What recorded result would justify changing tomorrow’s practice?
misconceptions.correction: Use predictions, attempts, and outcomes to choose one observable change and check it later.

content.title: Make a learning claim testable
content.body: Name one target, predict your later performance, and schedule a delayed recall plus one changed-context use. Keep the prediction beside the result.

content.prompt: Write an evidence plan for learning three terms today and checking them tomorrow.
content.solution: A defensible plan predicts a score, hides the terms for a delayed recall, and uses one term in a new sentence tomorrow.

content.title: Attempt before cueing
content.body: Cover the answer, attempt it, then reveal only a small cue. Put the next attempt on a later day and mix one nearby problem type.

content.prompt: Turn a formula you are learning into a two-session retrieval plan with one useful cue.
content.solution: Attempt the formula before seeing it, use a cue such as the quantity relationship only after the attempt, then return later with a related formula problem.

content.title: Read the signal in a struggle
content.body: When recall is effortful, mark the missing link, group the material by an explainable relationship, and try again later instead of using ease as a verdict.

criteria.label: Effort interpretation
criteria.description: Treats difficulty as information, not a conclusion.

criteria.label: Meaningful chunk
criteria.description: Names a relationship that organizes the material.

content.prompt: A learner rereads a four-step explanation until it feels easy but cannot explain step three later. Diagnose the next practice move.
content.solution: Do not treat ease as proof. Ask for the explanation from memory, identify the missing link, organize steps by why each follows, and check later.

content.title: Use support, then fade it
content.body: First explain each labelled step in a worked example. Next solve a similar case with labels removed. Finally classify any error and alter one condition for the retry.

criteria.label: Faded support
criteria.description: Moves from an example to a less-supported attempt.

criteria.label: Error-informed retry
criteria.description: Classifies an error and changes the retry.

content.prompt: Design three attempts after viewing a worked example of a new problem type.
content.solution: Attempt 1 annotates why each step works; attempt 2 removes the annotations; attempt 3 uses error feedback to choose a changed, similar problem.

content.title: Run your own next experiment
content.body: Support has faded: state a target, a practice condition, a later marker, and the one change you will make if the marker is weak.

criteria.label: Inspectable plan
criteria.description: Names target, condition, and later check.

criteria.label: Evidence-based reflection
criteria.description: Compares a record with a prediction.

content.title: One-week learning experiment
content.brief: Choose a small target, plan two practice attempts and a delayed marker, record what happened, then revise the next week’s condition.
content.deliverable: A short plan, result record, and one evidence-based revision.
rubric: The plan names a target and later evidence.
The reflection cites a record rather than a feeling alone.
The adaptation is specific enough to test.

references.citation: Koedinger, K. R., Corbett, A. T., & Perfetti, C. (2012). The Knowledge-Learning-Instruction framework: Bridging the science-practice chasm to enhance robust student learning.
